liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (4 reviews): Scarlet Begonias is called one of the best versions; paired with Music Never Stopped, the first set rocks; The band plays with ferocity from Scarlet Begonias onward [8][10][11][13]
- **Wharf Rat** (3 reviews): The Dancin' > Wharf Rat > Dancin' sequence is singled out as reason enough to download; The Dancin' > Wharf Rat > Dancin' sequence is described as magical [7][13][16]

## The recordings

- **gd1976-10-14.157426.aud.motb.0240.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 21 songs; 166 min [1]
- **gd76-10-14.sbd.cotsman.12614.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 155 min; rated 4/5 by 8 [2]. Said about its sound: Mostly fine audience recording; soundboard portions add inner detail, but reviewer prefers the audience version for feeling like the night [14]
- **gd76-10-14.bertrando.vernon.12079.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 157 min; rated 4.43/5 by 7 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording quality is merely decent and could be better, though the Dancin' > Wharf Rat > Dancin' sequence makes up for it; Reviewer calls this one of the best-sounding 1976 audience tapes; recommends SHN format, since compression hurts audience tapes more; Fine audience recording captures the feel of the night; soundboard portions only help with inner detail [7][10][15]
- **gd1976-10-14.168282.aud.bertrando.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 156 min [4]

## Around the show

- Phil seemed possessed in the first set; the second set is good but less killer than the first [8]
- Reviewer attended and recalls the mysterious ambience of the band and the Shrine, with Jerry playing superbly [12]
- The writer became a lifelong Deadhead during a second set, dated here as 15 October 1976 [19]
- Reviewer prefers the 15th and found this night's first set less engaging [13]
- Reviewer places the show in the lower tier of 1976 but still a nice show by Dead standards [14]
- Reviewer ranks the show in the lower tier for 1976, yet still nice by general Dead standards [15]
- The next night's show is slightly better; four songs from this show were repeated then and played better [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1976-10-14.157426.aud.motb.0240.flac16**: taped by Bob Menke; transferred by Transferred by: Bob Menke Mastering by: Derek McCabe; source: Analog Audience Source: Sony ECM 270 Microphones -> Sony TC 152SD Medium Stock Brands: Nakamichi CRO-2 tapes X 3 [1]
- **gd76-10-14.sbd.cotsman.12614.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard and Audience composite [2]. Also: Matrix mixes audience recording for set one with soundboard for set two and encore; Composite patched from Bertrando's audience recording and a soundboard source, transferred through several generations to SHN via Jeff Cotsman [2][8]
- **gd76-10-14.bertrando.vernon.12079.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Rob Bertrando; transferred by Marc Pujol; source: Audience Recording: Sony ECM-280s [3]
- **gd1976-10-14.168282.aud.bertrando.flac2496**: taped by Rob Bertrando; transferred by Rob Bertrando; source: Sony ECM-280's on balcony ledge right center> Sony TC-152SD > Sony TC-755 @3.75 ips [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1976-10-14 Thu Shrine Auditorium, Los Angeles, CA](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1415935685134/grateful-dead-1976-10-14-thu-shrine) [23]
